questions.question: A series is given, with one number missing. Choose the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series. 400, -200, 100, ? , 25, -12.5
questions.questionHtml:
A series is given, with one number missing. Choose the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

400, -200, 100, ? , 25, -12.5
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is: each number is divided by -2.

→ 400 ÷ (-2) = -200

→ -200 ÷ (-2) = 100

→ 100 ÷ (-2) = -50

→ -50 ÷ (-2) = 25

→ 25 ÷ (-2) = -12.5

→ -12.5

Hence, the missing number is -50 in the given series.

questions.question: Bhavin's birthday is on Monday 29th May. On what day of the week will be Rachit's Birthday in the same year if Rachit was born on 17th November?
questions.questionHtml: Bhavin's birthday is on Monday 29th May. On what day of the week will be Rachit's Birthday in the same year if Rachit was born on 17th November?
questions.solution:
Bhavin's birthday is on 29th May on Monday, so 2 days of May are remaining.

Therefore count rest of the days till the last date of that month as :

Remaining days of May → 2

June → 30

July → 31

August → 31

September → 30

October → 31

November → 17

Total days will be: 172

Now divide 172 by 7 (because 7 days in a week)

Remainder will be 4

Thus, 4 days after Monday will be Friday.

Hence, Rachit was born on Friday.

questions.question: The weights of 4 boxes are 30, 70, 60 and 90 kilograms. Which of the following cannot be the total weight, in kilograms, of any combination of these boxes and in a combination a box can be used only once?

questions.solution:
The combinations will be as follows:

90 + 70 + 60 + 30 = 250

90 + 70 + 30 = 190

90 + 70 + 60 = 220

But the combination of 200 is not possible.

Hence, 200 can’t be the total weight in kilograms.

questions.solution:

52 % 32 → (52 - 32) × 2 = 40

Similarly,

questions.question: Short run marginal cost curve cuts the average variable cost curve from _______ at the minimum point of average variable cost.
questions.questionHtml: Short run marginal cost curve cuts the average variable cost curve from _______ at the minimum point of average variable cost.
questions.solution: The solution states that the short-run marginal cost curve initially declines and then increases, intersecting the minimum points of the average total cost and average variable cost curves. questions.question: "Forests" is listed in the _________ list given in the Seventh Schedule in the Constitution of India.
questions.questionHtml: "Forests" is listed in the _________ list given in the Seventh Schedule in the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
Option 4 is correct, i.e. Concurrent.

  • Through the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 five subjects were transferred from State to Concurrent List.
  • They were:
    • Education
    • Forests
    • Weights & Measures
    • Protection of Wild Animals and Birds
    • Administration of Justice

Extra facts:

Seventh Schedule of the Indian constitution gives allocation of powers and functions between Union & States. It contains 3 lists:

  • Union List (For central Govt) 100 Subjects (originally 97).
  • States List (Powers of State Govt) 61 subjects  (originally 66). 
  • Concurrent List (Both Union & States) 52 subjects (originally 47).

questions.question: Name the Commission that came to India in 1928 to reform India's constitutional system.
questions.questionHtml: Name the Commission that came to India in 1928 to reform India's constitutional system.
questions.solution:
Option 4 is correct, i.e. Simon Commission.

  • The Simon Commission was formed in 1927 to fully assess India's political reforms.
  • The Simon Commission arrived in India on 3 February 1928.
  • There was no Indian leader in this commission, there was opposition to Simon Commission all over the country.
  • The commission consisted of seven members under the joint chairmanship of ​Sir John Simon, and Clement Attlee.

Extra facts:

  • Rowlatt Act:
    • In March 1919, the British Government passed the Rowlatt Act even though every single Indian member of the Central Legislative Council opposed it.
    • Three of them, Mohammed Ali Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya, and Mazhar-ul-Huq resigned their membership of the Council.
  • Partition of Bengal:
    • The first partition of Bengal was held on 19th July 1905.
    • It was announced by Lord Curzon who was the viceroy of India at that time.
    • The partition made two separate provinces, the Bengal and the Eastern Bengal which also contained Assam province.

questions.question: _________ is an example of intrusive igneous rock.
questions.questionHtml: _________ is an example of intrusive igneous rock.
questions.solution:
• Granite is an example of Intrusive Igneous Rocks.
  • Granite is a common type of felsic intrusive igneous rock that is granular and phaneritic in texture.
  • Granites can be predominantly white, pink, or grey in colour, depending on their mineralogy.
  • When molten magma cools it forms Igneous Rocks. 
  • There are two types of Igneous Rocks. They are:
    • Extrusive Igneous Rock.
    • Intrusive Igneous Rock.
  • Extrusive Igneous Rock: When Molten Lava reaches earth crust, it cools down rapidly and becomes solid and rocks formed in this process are called Extrusive Igneous Rock. Example: Basalt
  • Intrusive Igneous Rock: When Molten Magam cools down deep in the earth without reaching the earth surface, these types of rocks are called Intrusive Igneous Rock. Example: Granite 
  • Granite is an igneous rock that forms when magma cools relatively slowly underground. It is usually composed primarily of the minerals quartz, feldspar, and mica. When granite is subjected to intense heat and pressure, it changes into a metamorphic rock called gneiss.

questions.question: A multicellular organism grows by _________.
questions.questionHtml: A multicellular organism grows by _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Cell Division.

Key Points

  • All multicellular organisms use cell division for the growth and maintenance and repair of cells and tissues.
  • Few examples of multicellular organisms are human beings, plants, animals, birds, and insects.

Additional Information

  •  Cell division is the process by which a parent cell divides into two or more daughter cells.
  • There are two types of cell division: mitosis and meiosis.
  • Mitosis: The process cells use to make exact replicas of themselves. Mitosis is observed in almost all the body’s cells, including eyes, skin, hair, and muscle cells.
  • Meiosis: The is a process where a single cell divides twice to produce four cells containing half the original amount of genetic information. These cells are our sex cells.
  • Binary Fission: Single-celled organisms like bacteria replicate themselves for reproduction.

questions.question: Who discovered Circulatory System?
questions.questionHtml: Who discovered Circulatory System?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is William Harvey.

Key Points

  • William Harvey (1 April 1578 – 3 June 1657) was an English physician. 
  • He was the first known physician to describe the entire process of systemic circulation, including the property of blood being pumped to the body and brain by the heart and the rest of the body.
  • William Harvey discovered the circulation of blood.
  • William Harvey examines the arteries, demonstrating how their pulsation is controlled by the left ventricle's contraction, while the right ventricle's contraction propels blood into the pulmonary artery. 
  • He calculates the heart's capacity, the amount of blood expelled by each pump, and the number of times the heart beats in a half-hour.

Work done by A in 1 day is 1/12th of the total work

Work done by B in 1 day is 1/24th of the total work

According to the problem statement, work left can be given as

⇒ 1 - 4 × (1/12 + 1/24)

⇒ 1 - ½ = ½

∴ The ½ of the total work will be left

questions.question: What is the effective discount on two successive discounts of 20% and 25%?
questions.questionHtml: What is the effective discount on two successive discounts of 20% and 25%?
questions.solution:
Given:

The successive discount are 20% and 25%.

Formula used:

Successive discount = X + Y - (XY)/100

Where,

X = First discount

Y = Second discount

Calculation:

Successive discount = X + Y - (XY)/100

X = 20%, Y = 25%

⇒ 20 + 25 - 500/100

⇒ 45 - 5 = 40%

∴ The single equivalent discount is 40%.

 

Let the Selling price before discount be Rs. 100

Now the effective discount after 2 successive discounts can be given as

⇒ 100 × (1 - 20/100) (1 - 25/100) = 100 × 0.8 × 0.75

⇒ final selling price is Rs. 60

⇒ Discount is 100 - 60 = Rs. 40

∴ the discount percentage is 40%

questions.question: The average weight of P, Q and R is 47 kg. If the average weight of P and Q be 32.5 kg and that of Q and R be 48.5 kg, then what is the weight of Q (in kgs)?
questions.questionHtml: The average weight of P, Q and R is 47 kg. If the average weight of P and Q be 32.5 kg and that of Q and R be 48.5 kg, then what is the weight of Q (in kgs)?
questions.solution:
Let the weight of P, Q and R be p, q and r

According to the problem statement

⇒ (p + q + r)/3 = 47

⇒ p + q + r = 141    ----(i)

Now given that average weight of P and Q is 32.5 kg

⇒ (p + q) /2 = 32.5

⇒ p + q = 65 ----(ii)

Now, (i) - (ii)

⇒ r = 141 - 65 = 76    ----(iii)

Now given that average weight of Q and R is 48.5 kg

⇒ (q + r)/2 = 48.5

⇒ q + r = 97 Using (iii)

⇒ q = 97 - 76 = 21 kg

∴ the weight of q is 21 kg

questions.question: To cover a distance of 90 km in 2.5 hours what should be the average speed of the car in meters/second?

questions.question: If in 3 years at simple interest the principal increases by 18%, what will be the compound interest (in Rs) earned on Rs. 25,000 in 3 years at the same rate?
questions.questionHtml: If in 3 years at simple interest the principal increases by 18%, what will be the compound interest (in Rs) earned on Rs. 25,000 in 3 years at the same rate?
questions.solution:
Let the rate be r% and principle be p

According to the problem statement, since principle increases by 18% means interest is 0.18p

⇒ 0.18p = (p × r × 3) /100

⇒ r = 6%

Now CI can be given as

⇒ CI = 25000{(1 + 6/100) 3 - 1}

⇒ CI = 25000 × 0.191

⇒ CI = 4775.4

∴ CI is Rs. 4775.4

questions.question: If a + b = 1 and ab = -6, then what is the value of a 3 + b 3 ?

questions.solution:
Given:

a + b = 1 & ab = -6

(a + b) 3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

Calculation:

We know that

Put all the values given values

⇒ 13 = a3 + b3 + 3 × 3(- 6)

∴ The value of a3 + b3 is 19.

questions.question: The sum of a non - zero number and twenty times its reciprocal is 9. What is the number?
questions.questionHtml: The sum of a non - zero number and twenty times its reciprocal is 9. What is the number?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Check the options to satisfy the condition: Number + 20/Number = 9

Option (4): 5 + 20/5 ⇒ 5 + 4 = 9.

Condition satisfied.

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Alternate Method

Given: Sum of a non-zero number and 20 times its reciprocal is 9.

Formula Used: Let the number be x. Equation: x + 20(1/x) = 9

⇒ x + 20/x = 9

⇒ (x2 + 20) / x = 9

⇒ x2 + 20 = 9x

⇒ x2 − 9x + 20 = 0

⇒ x2 − 5x − 4x + 20 = 0

⇒ x(x − 5) − 4(x − 5) = 0

⇒ (x − 5)(x − 4) = 0

⇒ x = 5 or x = 4

From the given options, 5 is the correct choice.

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Additional Information

Quadratic Equation Roots

For ax2 + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a and the product of roots is c/a.

Reciprocal Relationship

If a number is x, its multiplicative inverse or reciprocal is 1/x, where x ≠ 0.

Nature of Roots

Discriminant D = b2 − 4ac helps determine if roots are real, equal, or imaginary.

questions.question: If the 3 rd and the 5 th term of an arithmetic progression are 13 and 21, what is the 13 th term?
questions.questionHtml: If the 3<sup>rd</sup> and the 5<sup>th</sup> term of an arithmetic progression are 13 and 21, what is the 13<sup>th</sup> term?
questions.solution:
Let the first term of AP be a and common difference be d

From the problem’s statement

⇒ 3rd term = a + (3 - 1) d = a + 2d = 13    ----(i)

⇒ 5th term = a + (5 - 1) d = a + 4d = 21    ----(ii)

Now (ii) - (i)

⇒ 2d = 8

⇒ d = 4, put this in (i)

⇒ a = 13 - 8 = 5

Now the 13th term can be given as a + 12d

⇒ 13th term = 5 + 12 × 4 = 53

∴ the 15th term of AP is 53

questions.question: Point P is the midpoint of segment AB. Co - ordinates of P are (5, -1) and A are (2, -4) . What are the co - ordinates of point B?
questions.questionHtml: Point P is the midpoint of segment AB. Co - ordinates of P are (5, -1) and A are (2, -4) . What are the co - ordinates of point B?
questions.solution:
Let coordinate of B be (x, y)

Since P is mid point so it can be written as

⇒ 5 = (2 + x) /2

⇒ x = 8

Now, for Y coordinate

⇒ -1 = (-4 + y) /2

⇒ y = 2

∴ the coordinates of B are (8, 2)

questions.question: What is the slope of the line perpendicular to the line passing through the points (-2, 3) and (2, 0)?
questions.questionHtml: What is the slope of the line perpendicular to the line passing through the points (-2, 3) and (2, 0)?
questions.solution:
Given:-

Points (-2, 3) and (2, 0)

Formula used:-

Slope of line which is passing through two points - 

Slope(m) = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1)

Slope of perpendicular line = -1/m

Calculation:-

According to the question -

Slope(m) = (0 - 3)/{2 - (-2)} = -3/4

∴ Slope of line perpendicular to given line = -1/(-3/4) = 4/3

∴ The required slope is 4/3

questions.question: ∆ABC is similar to ∆PQR. If ratio of perimeters of ∆ABC and ∆PQR is 1 : 2 and if PQ = 10 cm then what is the length of AB (in cm)?
questions.questionHtml: ∆ABC is similar to ∆PQR. If ratio of perimeters of ∆ABC and ∆PQR is 1 : 2 and if PQ = 10 cm then what is the length of AB (in cm)?
questions.solution:
Given:-

ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR and PQ = 10 cm

Perimeter of ΔABC/Perimeter of ΔPQR = 1/2

Formula used:-

Perimeter of ΔABC/Perimeter of ΔPQR = AB/PQ = BC/QR = AC/PR

Calculation:-  

According to the question -

⇒ Perimeter of ΔABC/Perimeter of ΔPQR = 1/2 = AB/PQ

⇒ AB = (1 × 10)/2

⇒ AB = 5 cm

∴ The required value of AB is 5 cm.

questions.question: If Sin θ = 12/13, then what is the value of Cot θ?
questions.questionHtml: If Sin θ = 12/13, then what is the value of Cot θ?
questions.solution:
Given:-

Sinθ = 12/13, so Cosecθ = 13/12

Formula used:-

Sinθ = Opposite/Hypotenuse = 1/Cosecθ 

Cotθ = √(Cosec2θ - 1)

Calculation:-

Cotθ can be written as

⇒ Cotθ = √(cosec2θ - 1)

= √(132/122 - 1)

= √{(169 - 144) /122}

= √(52/122)

⇒ Cotθ = 5/12

∴ Required value of Cotθ is 5/12 .

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given. Sultry
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.

Sultry
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The word "Sultry" means hot and humid; it often refers to weather conditions that are oppressively warm. (उमस भरा)
    • Example: The sultry summer afternoon made everyone feel lethargic.
  • "Frigid" refers to extremely cold conditions; it is the opposite of sultry. (कड़क ठंडा)
    • Example: The frigid winds of the Arctic are not suitable for most forms of life.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'sultry' is 'frigid'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Muggy (गर्म और नम): Unpleasantly warm and humid.
    • Example: The weather was muggy, making it hard to breathe.
  • Sticky (चिपचिपा): Having the properties of adhering or sticking to a surface.
    • Example: The sticky weather made my clothes cling to my skin.
  • Soggy (गीला): Soaked with moisture; wet and soft.
    • Example: The soggy ground made it difficult to walk through the field.

questions.solution:

Key Points

  • The word "Supple" means something that is flexible and can bend or fold easily without breaking. (लचीला)
    • Example: The gymnast's movements were so supple that she seemed to flow like water.
  • "Brittle" refers to something that is hard but liable to break or shatter easily. (भंगुर)
    • Example: The old, brittle branches snapped under the weight of the snow.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'Supple' is 'Brittle'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Brittle.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Flexible (लचीला): Capable of bending easily without breaking.
    • Example: The new material is very flexible and can be used in a variety of applications.
  • Pliable (नम्य): Easily bent or shaped.
    • Example: The metal wire is pliable enough to be twisted into any shape.
  • Bending (मुड़ने वाला): The action of changing the shape or direction of something.
    • Example: He demonstrated the bending strength of the new material.

questions.question: The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. They had been thrown X-upon their own exertions at an Y-battle to fight with poverty and ignorance Z-early age, and had a hard
questions.questionHtml:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

They had been thrown

X-upon their own exertions at an

Y-battle to fight with poverty and ignorance

Z-early age, and had a hard
questions.solution: The correct sequence would be XYZ. The first sentence ends with 'thrown', the only word that could be grammatically used after that is 'upon'. So the second sentece should be X. The second sentence ends with 'an; which means the third sentence should begin with a vowel. Therefore the third sentence would be Z which begins with 'early'. This would automatically make Y the last sentence.

questions.question: The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. The unstated assumption is X-conceding spatial autonomy Y-that the grant of a different time Z-zone is only the first temporal step towards
questions.questionHtml:
The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.

The unstated assumption is

X-conceding spatial autonomy 

Y-that the grant of a different time 

Z-zone is only the first temporal step towards
questions.solution: The sentence begins with an assertion and therefore the word 'that' must be used and therefore the second sentence should be Y. Now, Y ends with 'time' and Z begins with 'zone' which would automatically act as a clue so as to form the phrase 'time zone'. This would make Z the third sentence and by that extension X would become the fourth sentence.

questions.question: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. "What time will the flight arrive?" she asked the receptionist.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

"What time will the flight arrive?" she asked the receptionist.

options.text: She asked the receptionist what time the flight would arrive.
options.html: She asked the receptionist what time the flight would arrive.

options.text: She asked the receptionist what time the flight arrived.
options.html: She asked the receptionist what time the flight arrived.

options.text: She asked the receptionist when does the flight arrive
options.html: She asked the receptionist when does the flight arrive

options.text: She asked the receptionist what was going to be the time for the flights arrival
options.html: She asked the receptionist what was going to be the time for the flights arrival

questions.solution:
The correct answer is She asked the receptionist what time the flight would arrive.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the given question we have to change it into Indirect Speech. 
  • The process of transformation as follows: 
    • 'Said to' will be changed into 'Asked' because we know that the given sentence is interrogative with a question word. 
    • Comma and inverted commas will be removed. 
    • 'What' will be used as a conjunction because we know that in an interrogative sentence with a question word the question word itself becomes the conjunction. 
    • In indirect speech, an interrogative statement is converted into an assertive statement, so the auxiliary verb will come after the subject.
    • 'will' will be changed into 'would'. 
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1. 
    ​

Thus, the sentence becomes: She asked the receptionist what time the flight would arrive.
